study.article_kind: original mixed computational–in-vitro mechanical study with FE bone-growth/remodeling prediction
study.research_problem: Narrow dental implants can be mechanically vulnerable, while a stiff solid implant may concentrate load and contribute to marginal bone loss. The design challenge is to improve bone strain/ingrowth without sacrificing strength and initial stability in a 3.5 mm two-piece implant.
study.exact_gap: Prior work had considered porous Ti6Al4V implants or narrow implants separately; the authors state that biomechanical performance of small-diameter implants combining regional porosity had not been compared with both FE bone-remodeling analysis and mechanical testing.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Compare full-solid, upper-porous, lower-porous, lower-porous-upper-half, and lower-porous-lower-half 3.5 mm-diameter designs, using 3D FE simulations and in-vitro testing to identify a structure that balances stress tolerance, implant stability, and healthy marginal-bone strain under vertical and oblique loading.
study.study_design: Five 13 mm-long, 3.5 mm-diameter two-piece implant geometries were modeled in ANSYS with a 2 mm cortical layer and cancellous bone, friction coefficient 0.1, a ≤0.4 mm converged mesh, 150 N vertical or 150 N plus 20 N lateral oblique force, and six bone-growth/remodeling stages. The three primary designs (full solid, upper porous, lower porous) were laser-sintered from Ti6Al4V, tested under ISO 14801 dynamic loading and load–deformation, and inserted into Type-2 Sawbone blocks for Periotest stability measurements. FE stress/strain outputs and healthy/diseased bone fractions were compared with the physical behavior; no animal or patient study was performed.
study.sample_or_model: The virtual model uses SolidWorks/ANSYS geometries, titanium-alloy implant and abutment, cortical/cancellous bone, and fibrous tissue with homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic properties (Ti6Al4V 96,000 MPa, ν=0.36; cortical 10,700 MPa; cancellous 910 MPa; friction coefficient 0.1). Synthetic Type-2 bone had trabecular density 0.4 g/cm³ and modulus 759 MPa with a 2 mm cortical layer of 16.7 GPa. The Results figure reports N=11 for load–deformation/PTV summaries, but design allocation and exact specimen counts are not fully specified; S005 states at least three specimens per primary design met ISO 14801 without failure.
comparators: Full-solid, upper-porous, and lower-porous primary implants in mechanical testing, stability testing, and immediate FE stress analysis (S003:C01; S005:C01; S007:C01; S009:C01).
Lower-porous upper-half and lower-half variants in the FE bone-growth/remodeling simulations (S003:C01; S012:C01).
Vertical 150 N loading versus oblique loading with an additional 20 N lateral buccal-to-lingual force (S004:C01; S011:C01–S012:C01).
Stage 0–4 bone growth versus the post-surgery remodeling state, with healthy bone defined as bone-gain plus adapted strain and diseased bone as over-yield plus bone-loss strain (S004:C01; S012:C01).
Physical load tolerance and Periotest values across designs, including the upper-porous permanent-deformation threshold above 350 N (S009:C01–S010:C01).
method_spine: Design five regional-porosity implant bodies and two-piece assemblies modeled on a commercial 3.5 mm × 13 mm implant (S003:C01).
Build a converged three-dimensional FE model with cortical/cancellous bone, abutment/cap, frictional contacts, mesial/distal constraints, and vertical or oblique loads (S004:C01).
Simulate stages 0–4 of early bone filling and a post-surgery mechanostat remodeling state; classify ROI elements as healthy or diseased by strain categories (S004:C01).
Laser-sinter the three primary designs, conduct ISO 14801 loading/failure evaluation, and record load–deformation behavior (S005:C01; S009:C01).

Insert implants into Type-2 Sawbone blocks and measure mobility with Periotest; compare physical strength/stability with FE stress, strain, and marginal-bone fractions using medians/IQRs and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (S006:C01–S008:C01).

verification: A mesh size ≤0.4 mm was selected from convergence tests for the FE model (S004:C01).
Mechanical testing followed ISO 14801 procedures and at least three specimens per primary design reportedly passed without failure before subsequent experiments (S005:C01).
calibration: Material properties and bone-density inputs are assigned from literature or commercial Sawbone specifications; the FE model is not fitted to measured force, strain, or remodeling data (S004:C01; S006:C01).

The mechanostat/minimum-effective-strain categories are imported from prior theories and a previous algorithm, not calibrated against this study's histology or longitudinal bone measurements (S004:C01; S013:C01).
validation: Physical load–deformation/failure behavior and Periotest stability provide in-vitro mechanical checks for the three primary laser-sintered designs, including observed upper-porous deformation above 350 N (S005:C01; S007:C01; S009:C01–S010:C01).

The packet does not report a direct quantitative comparison between FE stress/strain fields and measured surface strains, nor any biological, animal, or clinical validation of the remodeling predictions (S004:C01; S013:C01–S013:C02).
sensitivity: Porosity location/amount, loading orientation, and six bone-growth/remodeling states form a design and state sweep; the reduced-porosity subtypes test whether the bone benefit persists when porous volume is shortened (S003:C01; S011:C01–S012:C01).
No formal uncertainty, parameter, fatigue-life, friction, sliding, anisotropy, or geometry sensitivity analysis is reported beyond the mesh convergence check.
application_prediction: FE healthy/diseased bone fractions and stress maps predict how each idealized design may redistribute load or support marginal bone under the specified static loads and remodeling rule (S011:C01–S012:C01).

Statements that lower porosity is clinically desirable, upper porosity is unsuitable, or a design improves bone integration are bounded by the synthetic-bone tests and model proxies; no in-vivo osseointegration or patient outcome was measured (S013:C01–S013:C02).

primary_outcomes: Mechanical load–deformation tolerance ranked full solid highest, lower porous next, and upper porous lowest; all three PTV groups showed excellent stability, but full solid and upper porous were more stable than lower porous, which had the least stability (S009:C01).

Upper-porous implants showed permanent deformation above 350 N and a crooked internal screw after cap removal, localizing the failure to a stress-concentrating solid–porous geometric discontinuity (S009:C01–S010:C01).

Under vertical 150 N FE loading, cortical-bone maximum stress was highest for upper porous at 131.38 MPa; implant maximum stress was 872.13 MPa for upper porous versus 97.81 MPa full solid and 122.54 MPa lower porous. Oblique loading increased magnitude and shifted stress opposite the applied force; upper porous reached 1315.2 MPa in the implant body (S011:C01).

The lower-porous implant produced a more uniform cancellous-bone stress pattern than full solid or upper porous while retaining similar cortical/cancellous stress magnitudes to full solid (S011:C01; S013:C01).

At the first three threads under vertical Stage 0, healthy-bone fractions were 69.5% full solid, 78.2% upper porous, and 74.3% lower porous; under oblique loading they were 57.3%, 65.7%, and 59.0%, respectively (S012:C01).

After simulated post-surgery remodeling, first-three-thread healthy fractions fell to 45.5% full solid, 64.0% upper porous, and 56.9% lower porous under vertical load, and to 48.6%, 61.2%, and 51.3% under oblique load; the reduced-porosity upper-half/lower-half variants were generally lower still (S012:C01).

The model therefore predicts the strongest marginal-bone proxy for upper porous but the physical deformation and >1300 MPa stress concentration make it unsuitable under the tested small-diameter loading; lower porous offers a compromise of near-full-solid strength and higher marginal healthy-bone fraction, while reducing porous volume attenuates the regeneration proxy (S013:C01–S013:C02).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: In-vitro mechanical/stability evidence combined with FE stress and mechanostat-based bone-remodeling predictions; no biological, animal, or clinical validation of bone ingrowth or long-term survival.

argument_map.central_claim: For the tested 3.5 mm two-piece Ti6Al4V designs, lower regional porosity preserves mechanical tolerance close to full solid while improving the modeled marginal-bone strain distribution, whereas upper porosity gives the best healthy-bone proxy but fails by junctional stress/deformation above 350 N; decreasing porous volume weakens the bone-regeneration proxy.
data: Five idealized regional-porosity geometries and vertical/oblique FE load cases with six bone-growth/remodeling states (S003:C01–S004:C01).
Laser-sintered full-solid, upper-porous, and lower-porous implants tested for load tolerance and Periotest stability, with upper-porous permanent deformation above 350 N (S005:C01–S010:C01).
FE implant/bone stress maps and healthy/diseased fractions at the marginal first three threads, including Stage 0 and post-remodeling comparisons (S011:C01–S012:C01).
argument_map.warrant: The combined physical and FE results support a conditional mechanical–bone-strain trade-off among these configurations; healthy/diseased fractions remain mechanostat proxies and do not demonstrate histologic ingrowth, durable fixation, or clinical prevention of marginal bone loss.
backing: The upper-porous failure mode is observed in both FE stress concentration and physical permanent deformation/crooked screw, providing convergent evidence for a junctional weakness (S010:C01; S011:C01; S013:C01).

Lower porous has similar reported stress tolerance to full solid, a more uniform cancellous stress map, and higher first-three-thread healthy fractions than full solid across the stated model states (S009:C01; S011:C01; S012:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Evidence applies to idealized 3.5 mm × 13 mm Ti6Al4V designs, Type-2 Sawbone blocks, ISO-style static/dynamic loading and 150 N/20 N FE loads, homogeneous isotropic material assumptions, and the specified mechanostat categories.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Lower porous was least stable by PTV despite near-full-solid load tolerance, so strength and initial stability do not identify one universally best design (S009:C01).

Upper porous has the best marginal healthy-bone fraction but reaches 872.13 MPa vertical and 1315.2 MPa oblique implant stress and deforms above 350 N; biological and mechanical criteria conflict (S011:C01; S013:C01).
The FE bone model uses simplified homogeneous/isotropic bone and static vertical/oblique forces; chewing, sliding, friction evolution, anisotropy, and complex anatomy are omitted (S013:C02).
Only three primary designs were physically tested, specimen allocation is unclear, and no animal or patient endpoint validates the remodeling fractions (S005:C01; S009:C01).
argument_map.argument_coherence: moderate_to_high for the in-vitro mechanical trade-off and conditional FE comparison; moderate for bone-ingrowth and clinical implications

measured: Laser-sintered Ti6Al4V full-solid, upper-porous, and lower-porous assemblies were subjected to ISO 14801-style loading; load–deformation tolerance and an upper-porous permanent-deformation/crooked-screw failure were observed (S005:C01; S009:C01–S010:C01).
Periotest mobility values were measured after insertion into Type-2 Sawbone blocks; all three designs were described as stable, with lower porous least stable (S006:C01; S007:C01; S009:C01).
Synthetic-bone density and elastic moduli are commercial specimen inputs, not human bone measurements (S006:C01).
predicted: FE implant, cortical-bone, and cancellous-bone stress distributions under 150 N vertical and 150 N + 20 N oblique loads (S011:C01).
Healthy/diseased bone volume fractions for five designs across Stages 0–4 and the post-surgery remodeling state (S012:C01).
Design-level claims that lower porous balances mechanical strength and marginal-bone strain, and that reduced porous volume weakens the regeneration proxy (S012:C01–S013:C02).
inferred: The upper-porous junction is inferred to be the causal weakness because its sharp solid–porous discontinuity coincides with the FE stress maximum and observed crooked-screw deformation (S010:C01; S011:C01).

Higher healthy-bone fractions near the first three threads are inferred to indicate more favorable bone ongrowth/ingrowth, but they are mechanostat classifications rather than measured tissue (S004:C01; S012:C01).

Lower porous is inferred to be more clinically desirable than upper porous because it retains tolerance and improves the model's marginal-bone proxy; this remains conditional on the simplified loading and synthetic-bone setup (S013:C01).
recommended: Repeat testing with clearly reported specimen allocation, as-built porosity and surface metrology, fatigue cycles, and direct FE-to-experiment strain comparisons.
Use anatomical, heterogeneous, anisotropic, viscoelastic bone models and dynamic chewing with sliding/friction to test whether the trade-off persists (S013:C02).
Validate bone-ingrowth/remodeling predictions with histology, imaging, animal time courses, and patient-relevant marginal-bone outcomes before clinical selection.
Test hybrid connection geometries or materials that reduce upper-porous junction stress without losing the porous region's modeled bone benefit (S013:C01–S013:C02).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Load–deformation tolerance and Periotest values indicate in-vitro mechanical behavior and initial mobility, not long-term fatigue survival or osseointegration.
FE stress concentration identifies a candidate failure location, not observed clinical fracture, screw loosening, or peri-implantitis.
Healthy/diseased strain fractions are model-defined mechanostat proxies, not bone volume, histologic ingrowth, bone–implant contact, or marginal bone loss measured in vivo.
Synthetic Sawbone does not reproduce living bone remodeling, vascularity, anisotropy, viscoelasticity, or biologic interface formation.
Static vertical/oblique loads do not establish behavior under cyclic mastication, sliding, wear, corrosion, or years of function.
overclaim_risks: The Conclusion states that porous structure significantly enhances post-implantation bone ongrowth/ingrowth although no living tissue was measured and the fractions come from FE strain categories (S013:C02).
Calling lower porous clinically desirable extrapolates from a synthetic-bone stability/mechanical compromise and a simplified model to patient outcomes (S009:C01; S013:C01).
The upper-porous unsuitability claim is strong for the tested >350 N deformation/junction geometry but should not be generalized to redesigned connections or other diameters/materials.

The reduction in porous proportion is interpreted as adverse bone regeneration although the result is sensitive to the assumed mechanostat rule, bone geometry, loads, and stage definitions (S012:C01–S013:C02).

section_moves.move: Use the stress-shielding versus fixation trade-off to define the small-diameter porous-design gap and comparator set.
section_moves.execution: The Introduction connects marginal bone loss and modulus mismatch to prior isoelastic implants, then states the unstudied combination of narrow diameter and regional porosity and the FE-plus-mechanical objective (S002:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: End an implant-design introduction with the exact diameter, porosity factors, loading/validation plan, and primary mechanical and tissue-proxy endpoints.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not infer that modulus matching alone solves fixation or bone loss; the RM isoelastic example shows the adverse consequences of poor ingrowth and micromotion.

section_moves.move: Align the virtual and physical setups before interpreting design differences.
section_moves.execution: The methods specify geometry, material/contact assumptions, vertical/oblique forces, remodeling stages, laser-sintered specimens, ISO loading, Sawbone composition, Periotest, and rank-sum statistics (S003:C01–S008:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For mixed FE–experimental implant work, state which designs are physically fabricated, which are virtual-only, what each test measures, and where model inputs differ from living bone.
section_moves.failure_mode: A converged FE mesh and ISO protocol cannot compensate for synthetic-bone and homogeneous-material assumptions when claiming biological performance.

section_moves.move: Report physical strength/stability first, then FE stress, then remodeling fractions so failure and trade-offs remain visible.
section_moves.execution: Results begin with load–deformation/PTV and the upper-porous failure, then give immediate stress fields and finally healthy/diseased fractions across stages and loads (S009:C01–S012:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Separate measured mechanical behavior from model-level tissue predictions and retain conflicting metrics such as lower-porous stability versus strength.
section_moves.failure_mode: Selecting the design with the highest healthy-bone proxy while omitting its >350 N deformation would hide the central trade-off.

section_moves.move: Use the observed junction failure to explain the FE stress map, then reconcile upper-porous bone benefit with mechanical unsuitability and lower-porous compromise.
section_moves.execution: The Discussion links upper-porous discontinuity to deformation, compares lower porous with full solid, and reports the decline in healthy fractions during post-surgery remodeling before stating simplified-model and static-load limitations (S013:C01–S013:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A mixed-study Discussion should let convergent physical and FE failure evidence constrain biological interpretation, then state what experiment would test the proxy bridge.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not treat a mechanostat fraction as equivalent to histologic ingrowth or a static load as clinical mastication.

section_moves.move: Close with the conditional design trade-off and list dynamic/biological work before clinical translation.
section_moves.execution: The Conclusion retains upper-porous bone integration versus reduced stress resistance and lower-porosity loss of regeneration, then proposes advanced materials, hybrid structures, biological models, and dynamic loads (S013:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A conclusion should state the tested mechanical compromise, preserve the evidence state of bone predictions, and place in-vivo and dynamic validation in future work.
section_moves.failure_mode: Phrases such as significantly enhances bone ongrowth/ingrowth require qualification when the endpoint is a simulated strain category.

author_reported: The bone geometry and material model are simplified and do not capture inhomogeneity, anisotropy, viscoelasticity, or the full complexity of remodeling (S013:C01–S013:C02).
Only static vertical and oblique occlusal forces were applied; chewing, sliding, and friction should be incorporated in future work (S013:C02).
Future studies should use more sophisticated geometry/material models, biological models, dynamic loading, and advanced or hybrid materials (S013:C01–S013:C02).
reader_identified: Synthetic Sawbone and short-term in-vitro testing cannot validate living bone ingrowth, remodeling, peri-implantitis, or long-term fixation.
The exact sample allocation is unclear: the figure reports N=11, while the methods only state at least three specimens per primary design passed ISO loading.
Only full-solid, upper-porous, and lower-porous designs were physically fabricated/tested; the two reduced-porosity variants are FE-only.
No direct quantitative FE-to-measured strain or stress validation, uncertainty propagation, fatigue-life result, or as-built porosity/metrology is reported.
The 0.1 friction coefficient, homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity, fixed mesial/distal constraints, and static 150 N/20 N loads may strongly shape the ranking.
likely_bias_direction: Mechanostat thresholds and homogeneous FE inputs likely make healthy/diseased fractions appear more precise and transferable than living bone behavior allows.
The synthetic block and static loading may understate biologic variability, interface slip, chewing fatigue, wear, and corrosion.
The preferred lower-porous compromise may be biased by not measuring biological ingrowth or by not isolating porosity from connection geometry and stability.
Upper-porous failure is likely specific to the sharp junction and 3.5 mm geometry; generalizing it to all upper-porous designs would bias against redesigned interfaces.
limitations.scope_boundary: The evidence supports conditional comparison of five regional-porosity designs for a 3.5 mm two-piece Ti6Al4V implant under the stated FE loads and synthetic-bone mechanical tests. It does not demonstrate in-vivo bone ingrowth, marginal-bone preservation, fatigue life, corrosion/wear resistance, long-term fixation, peri-implantitis prevention, or patient benefit.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate measured mechanical/stability outcomes from FE mechanostat predictions, and state the proxy-to-bone bridge explicitly before making a design recommendation.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Mixed FE–experimental Results, Discussion, and Conclusion audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A direct histologic or imaging endpoint could strengthen the bridge; simulated healthy-bone fractions alone cannot establish ingrowth or clinical preservation.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Use convergent failure evidence—FE stress concentration plus observed permanent deformation/crooked screw—to constrain a biological design claim, while retaining discordant stability metrics.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Failure-mode Results, design-selection Discussion, and comparator audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: The junction mechanism is specific to the tested geometry until reproduced across redesigned interfaces, diameters, materials, and loading histories.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Report a complete porosity-by-location and loading-orientation matrix, preserving adverse remodeling changes and the fact that lower stability can coexist with near-full-solid strength.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: When specimen allocation or physical testing is incomplete, do not imply that the virtual reduced-porosity variants received the same validation as the three primary designs.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Treat ISO compliance and mesh convergence as bounded verification/physical checks, not as validation of long-term mastication, living remodeling, fatigue, or clinical outcomes.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods validation ledger and translational boundary.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Living-tissue imaging, histology, longitudinal mechanics, or patient data would be needed to move beyond the in-vitro/model rung.

quality.validation_credibility: moderate for in-vitro mechanical behavior; low_to_moderate for direct FE and remodeling validation
quality.outcome_uncertainty_reporting: moderate for PTV/strain summaries but low for model uncertainty and fatigue
quality.comparator_fairness: moderate for the three primary designs; lower for virtual-only reduced-porosity variants and biological extrapolation
critical_weaknesses: Synthetic Sawbone and no in-vivo or clinical tissue endpoint.
Simplified homogeneous/isotropic bone and static loading omit anatomy, chewing, sliding, and biologic variability.
Unclear specimen allocation (N=11 figure versus at least three per design) and only three primary designs physically tested.
No direct quantitative FE-to-experiment field validation, as-built porosity metrology, or complete fatigue outcome.
Mechanostat healthy/diseased fractions are proxies that are used to support bone-ingrowth language.
quality.overall_credibility: moderate for the reported in-vitro mechanical trade-off and conditional FE stress patterns; low_to_moderate for remodeling, osseointegration, and clinical claims

summary_zh: 这是一项将有限元、体外机械试验和骨生长/重塑预测结合的原创小直径牙种植体研究。作者比较 3.5 mm 直径、13 mm 长的全实心、上部多孔、下部多孔以及下部多孔上下半段变体；三种主要设计用激光烧结 Ti6Al4V 制备，按 ISO 14801 进行加载/失效评价，并在 Type-2 Sawbone 中用 Periotest 测稳定性。FE 模型使用 ≤0.4 mm 网格、150 N 垂直和额外 20 N 斜向载荷，模拟 Stage 0–4 骨生长及术后 mechanostat 重塑。上部多孔的边界应力最高（垂直 872.13 MPa、斜向 1315.2 MPa），超过 350 N 出现永久变形和内螺钉弯曲；但其前三螺纹健康骨比例最高。下部多孔强度接近全实心、应力更均匀、边缘健康骨比例高于全实心，却具有较低的 Periotest 稳定性；减少多孔体积后，重塑模型中的健康骨比例下降。最稳妥的结论是存在机械强度、初始稳定性和 mechanostat 骨代理终点之间的条件性权衡，不能把合成骨和 FE 健康比例当作活体骨长入、边缘骨丢失或临床获益。
reader_notes: Primary Luna reader read every non-reference locator in order: S001:C01 through S013:C01, S013:C02, S014:C01, S015:C01, and S016:C01; all 17 packet headings were read and omissions are none.
Full-text classification confirms mixed computational and in-vitro mechanical research; animal/clinical/biological cue labels do not represent completed study arms.

Physical ISO/Sawbone outcomes, FE stress fields, and mechanostat healthy/diseased fractions were kept in separate evidence states; the N=11 versus at-least-three-per-design allocation ambiguity was retained.
Self-review retained the upper-porous failure, lower-porous lower stability, post-remodeling declines, synthetic-bone and static-load limitations, and the absent in-vivo bone-ingrowth endpoint.
